title: Marla, Kanal and Square Feet: Land Measurement in Pakistan Explained
description: How big is a marla, a kanal and an acre? Learn the standard sizes in square feet and square yards, how to convert them, and the mistakes buyers make.
lead: How big is a marla, a kanal and an acre? Learn the standard sizes in square feet and square yards, how to convert them, and the mistakes buyers make.
body:
Plots in Pakistan are sold in marla and kanal, while building plans, bank valuations and tax papers often use square feet or square yards. Knowing how the units relate saves you from paying for land you do not get.

The standard sizes

  • 1 marla = 272.25 square feet = 30.25 square yards (the size used in most of Pakistan)
  • 1 kanal = 20 marla = 5,445 square feet
  • 1 acre = 160 marla = 8 kanal = 43,560 square feet
  • 1 square yard = 9 square feet

So a 5 marla plot is 1,361.25 square feet, a 10 marla plot is 2,722.5 square feet and a 1 kanal plot is 5,445 square feet.

Not every marla is the same

In India and Bangladesh a marla is defined as 25 square yards, which is 225 square feet. Some local land records and housing schemes in Pakistan also use their own sizes. Before you pay, ask which marla the seller means and check it against the registry or fard.

Worked example

A seller offers a "10 marla" plot. At 272.25 square feet per marla it measures 2,722.5 square feet, or 302.5 square yards, which is half a kanal. If the seller is counting 225 square feet per marla, the plot is only 2,250 square feet, almost 20 percent smaller.

Land area is not covered area

A plot's land area is the ground you own. Covered area is the built-up floor area, which can be larger on a double-storey house. Compare like with like when you price a property.

Tips before you buy

  • Get the area in square feet in writing.
  • Check the measured area in the registry, fard or approved map, not only the advertisement.
  • Confirm the marla size used in that scheme.
  • Make sure the seller's tax and NTN details are in order before the transfer.

To convert quickly, use our free Marla, Kanal and Square Feet Converter. You can change the marla size if your area uses a different one.

Sources: Wikipedia, "Marla (unit)". Always confirm the area of a specific plot with its official records.
